summary: Verified create() calls assertCanAssignRole before roleResolver.resolveOrThrow/repo.save (line order 83 -> 86 -> 98), confirmed by users-create-role-authority.security.spec.ts asserting resolveOrThrow NOT called when the check throws. actorRole defaults to 'viewer' (level 10) when @CurrentMember() is undefined; since no real role has hierarchy_level<10 and the hierarchy check rejects targetLevel>=actorLevel for non-owner/super_admin actors, an undefined actor fails closed for every real target role. Exhaustive grep of apps/api/src for org_members role/role_id writers found only: users.service.ts (now guarded), workspace-provisioning.service.ts (hardcodes role='owner' on brand-new tenant creation, not attacker-controlled -> non-issue), bootstrap-tenant-zero.ts (CLI-only, not HTTP-reachable -> system-context), and migrations/seeds (system/migration-only). Investigated a theoretical alias/canonical_role_id bypass (assertCanAssignRole checks the alias row's own hierarchy/is_assignable while resolveOrThrow follows canonical_role_id to a possibly different row) but confirmed non-exploitable: the only two seeded aliases (artista->artist, tenant_owner->owner) have matching hierarchy_level and is_assignable to their canonical target, and rbac-mutation.service.createRole never accepts/sets canonical_role_id for tenant-created custom roles, so no attacker-reachable path can create a low-privilege-looking alias pointing to a higher-privilege canonical role. Confirmed env.schema.ts staging gate and ai-jobs/external-data processor tenant-context diffs are untouched working-tree changes, unaffected by this users-module-scoped round. No reproducible issue found.
